content.text:
Dashboard analyzed. Here's my take, with the frontend-design / UI-wiki / electron / angular-developer lenses applied.

## What I observed (screenshots + code)

**Current dashboard** ([workspace-dashboard.component.ts](libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/workspace-dashboard.component.ts), [dashboard-layout.service.ts](libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-layout.service.ts)):

- 5 widget types, 3 enabled by default: Continue Watching (full), Recently Watched (2/3), Global Favorites (1/3). Source Stats + Recently Added hidden.
- Edit mode (top-right `tune`) reveals: drag handles, size stepper with **4 sizes** (1/3, 1/2, 2/3, full), per-widget hide button, and a 380px right-side library panel with on/off toggles.
- Widgets also have **their own** view mode toggle (list/grid) and kind filter (all/channels/VOD/series), each persisted separately in localStorage.
- Fixed `--dashboard-widget-height: 400px` for most slots. 12-column grid with a dashed overlay grid visible while editing.
- Dashboard empty state when all widgets are hidden: bland text "No widgets enabled" — not onboarding-grade.
- **No first-run / no-playlist experience on the dashboard itself.** The beautiful illustrated `EmptyStateComponent` exists ([empty-state.component.html](libs/playlist/shared/ui/src/lib/recent-playlists/empty-state/empty-state.component.html)) but only renders in Sources view.

Screenshots: default view and edit mode (edit mode shows the dashed 12-col overlay, size stepper 1/3-1/2-2/3-full, and the right-side widget library panel).

## Recommendation: simplify to a rail-based layout

**Short answer: yes, redesign.** Your users come from Netflix / Apple TV / YouTube mental models — "rows of posters I scroll through," not "dashboard I lay out like Notion." The current grid has four customization surfaces per widget (drag, resize stepper 4-way, hide, per-widget view/filter) and still produces mediocre layouts, because the content (posters, titles, metadata) has a natural shape that doesn't benefit from 1/3 vs 2/3 columns.

### What to keep
- The widget *content* (Continue Watching, Recently Watched, Favorites, Recently Added, Source Stats).
- The Continue Watching hero pattern — it's the strongest element.
- Material 3 tokens + the tinted glass surfaces (frontend-design-aligned, tasteful).
- Per-rail kind filter (all / live / vod / series) — useful, low-cost.

### What to remove
- **4 size variants** (one-third / half / two-thirds / full) → every rail is full-width.
- **Drag-drop reorder + show/hide toggles** → curated static order. Auto-hide a rail when its data is empty (already trivial via `computed`).
- **Edit mode + right-side library panel + 380px sidebar** → delete entire mode. The `tune` icon can become a small menu with two switches max ("Show tips / Compact rows") or be removed.
- **Per-widget list vs grid toggle** → pick one per rail and commit. "Recently Watched" = grid, "Source stats" = compact strip.
- **Fixed 400px widget height** → rails size to poster aspect ratio (~2:3 for movies, 16:9 for live).
- **12-column grid overlay** while editing — gone with edit mode.

### Redesigned structure

```
┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Good evening, <user>           [⚙ Settings]              │  ← lightweight header
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  ▶ Continue Watching — Private TV · edem/ilook · 1h ago  │  ← hero (big card)
│  [ big poster ]      [ Resume ▶ ]                         │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Recently watched                            See all →    │
│  [card][card][card][card][card][card] →→                  │  ← horizontal rail, scroll-snap
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Global favorites                            See all →    │
│  [card][card][card] →→                                    │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Recently added                              See all →    │
│  [card][card][card][card] →→                              │
├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Sources  3 playlists · 93,412 channels · 3 favorites     │  ← compact strip, not a card grid
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

### First-run / empty dashboard

Reuse [empty-state.component.html](libs/playlist/shared/ui/src/lib/recent-playlists/empty-state/empty-state.component.html) *welcome* variant on the dashboard when `playlists.length === 0`. Current SVG illustration + three feature tiles (M3U / Xtream / Stalker) + one primary CTA is already on-brand. Promote it to a shared `libs/ui/components` export and render it via `@if (!hasPlaylists()) { <app-empty-state type="welcome" /> }` before the rails.

### Angular / state (angular-developer lens)

Replace `DashboardLayoutService` + version 14 localStorage migrations with a thin `computed`:

```ts
readonly rails = computed<Rail[]>(() => {
  const all = this.data.globalRecentItems();
  const favs = this.data.globalFavoriteItems();
  return [
    { id: 'continue', kind: 'hero', item: all[0] },
    { id: 'recent', kind: 'rail', items: all },
    { id: 'favorites', kind: 'rail', items: favs },
    ...
  ].filter(r => r.kind === 'hero' ? r.item : r.items.length > 0);
});
```

No persistence. No migrations. The rail component owns its own scroll position.

### UI-wiki details worth adopting
- **Scroll-snap**: `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory; scroll-padding-inline-start: 20px` on rails + `scroll-snap-align: start` on cards so keyboard/arrow nav lands on card boundaries.
- **Fade-in chevrons** on hover for desktop (Electron), hidden on touch. Not auto-showing — avoids Netflix's "always-on chevrons" clutter.
- **Image loading**: you already use `loading="lazy"` — add `decoding="async"` and a fixed aspect-ratio wrapper to prevent CLS.
- **Skeletons**: one shimmer per card (not a single widget-wide spinner) — keeps layout stable while loading.

### Electron lens
Your current Electron window rendered at ~720×460 in my screenshots — that's too narrow for any rail layout. Bump the default `BrowserWindow` size to 1280×800 and set `minWidth: 960` so rails don't collapse to a single card. Rails without breathing room defeat the whole pattern.

## Net impact
- ~**-300 lines** of dashboard code (layout service, migrations, sidebar editor, size logic, grid overlay SCSS).
- ~**-3 localStorage keys** per widget.
- **Zero** "how do I configure this" questions from users.
- A UI that matches modern streaming conventions and looks like a product instead of a configurable dashboard.

Want me to build a proof-of-concept rail layout (one new component + reusing `EmptyStateComponent` for the welcome state) so you can compare side-by-side before committing to the simplification?

## angular-cli

<General Purpose>
This server provides a safe, programmatic interface to the Angular CLI for an AI assistant.
Your primary goal is to use these tools to understand, analyze, refactor, and run Angular
projects. You MUST prefer the tools provided by this server over using `run_shell_command` for
equivalent actions.
</General Purpose>

<Core Workflows & Tool Guide>
* **1. Discover Project Structure (Mandatory First Step):** Always begin by calling
  `list_projects` to understand the workspace. The `path` property for a workspace
  is a required input for other tools.

* **2. Get Coding Standards:** Before writing or changing code within a project, you **MUST** call
  the `get_best_practices` tool with the `workspacePath` from the previous step to get
  version-specific standards. For general knowledge, you can call the tool without this path.

* **3. Answer User Questions:**
    - For conceptual questions ("what is..."), use `search_documentation`.
    - For code examples ("show me how to..."), use `find_examples`.
</Core Workflows & Tool Guide>

<Key Concepts>
* **Workspace vs. Project:** A 'workspace' contains an `angular.json` file and defines 'projects'
  (applications or libraries). A monorepo can have multiple workspaces.
* **Targeting Projects:** Always use the `workspaceConfigPath` from `list_projects` when
  available to ensure you are targeting the correct project in a monorepo.
</Key Concepts>

## nx-mcp

The Nx MCP server provides tools for working with Nx monorepo workspaces. Use it to:

  - Understand workspace architecture, project dependencies, and configuration
  - Retrieve up-to-date Nx documentation for configuration questions and best practices
  - Explore individual project details, targets, and how to run them
  - Discover available generators and scaffold new code
  - Visualize project and task dependency graphs
  - Monitor running tasks and view their output
  - Analyze CI/CD pipeline performance and history from Nx Cloud
  - Interact with Nx Cloud self-healing CI

  Any kind of work inside the Nx workspace or monorepo as well when working with CI can make use of the Nx MCP server.

## plugin:context7:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service -- even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer -- your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, writing scripts from scratch, debugging business logic, code review, or general programming concepts.

**Route**: [http://localhost:4200/workspace/dashboard-rails](http://localhost:4200/workspace/dashboard-rails) (sibling to `/workspace/dashboard`, no guard, no interference with the existing dashboard).

**Files added** (all under 300 lines each per CLAUDE.md):

- [libs/playlist/shared/ui/src/index.ts](libs/playlist/shared/ui/src/index.ts) — export `EmptyStateComponent` (reuse for welcome)
- [libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/index.ts](libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/index.ts) — export new components
- [apps/web/src/app/app.routes.ts](apps/web/src/app/app.routes.ts:47) — added `dashboard-rails` child route

- i18n keys for `RECENT_SOURCES` title on the playlists rail (using existing key, falls back OK)
- Replacing `/workspace/dashboard` wholesale — current POC is additive so you can compare
- Tests for the new components

If you like the direction, next step is to swap the route (`dashboard` → rails component) and delete `DashboardLayoutService`, the widget library panel, the editor SCSS, and the 4 per-widget view/filter localStorage keys — ~500 LOC net deletion.

# Workspace Dashboard

This document records the current dashboard implementation inside the workspace
shell. It replaces the earlier dashboard plan document.

Related:

- [Workspace Shell](./workspace-shell.md)

## Summary

- The dashboard is the default `/workspace` landing page.
- It is a widget-based surface with persisted layout and widget settings.
- The current implementation favors a constrained, stable layout over a full
  freeform grid system.

Core implementation:

1. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/workspace-dashboard.component.ts`
2. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/workspace-dashboard.component.html`
3. `libs/workspace/dashboard/ui/src/lib/dashboard-widget-host.component.ts`
4. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-widget.model.ts`
5. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-layout.service.ts`
6. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-data.service.ts`

## Current Widget Set

Registered widget types:

1. `source-stats`
2. `continue-watching`
3. `recently-watched`
4. `global-favorites`

Default layout:

1. `continue-watching`
    1. Enabled by default
    2. Size `full`
2. `recently-watched`
    1. Enabled by default
    2. Size `two-thirds`
    3. Scope-aware
3. `global-favorites`
    1. Enabled by default
    2. Size `one-third`
    3. Scope-aware
4. `source-stats`
    1. Present in the registry
    2. Disabled by default

53	The old refactor summary mentioned `Recent Sources`, but that widget is not in

55	
56	## Layout And Persistence Contract
57	
58	The dashboard persists a versioned layout object in local storage.
59	
60	Current storage details:
61	
62	1. Storage key: `workspace-dashboard-layout-v3`
63	2. Schema version: `12`
64	3. Size presets:
65	    1. `one-third`
66	    2. `half`
67	    3. `two-thirds`
68	    4. `full`
69	4. Scope settings:
70	    1. `providers: Array<'m3u' | 'xtream' | 'stalker'>`
71	    2. `playlistIds: string[]`
72	
73	Normalization rules in `DashboardLayoutService`:
74	
75	1. Stored widgets are merged against `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_WIDGETS`.
76	2. Missing widgets are restored from defaults.
77	3. Removed or invalid settings fall back to normalized defaults.
78	4. Titles and descriptions come from the current code-defined defaults, not
79	   stale stored values.
80	5. Widget order is reindexed after normalization.
81	
82	## Rendering Flow
83	
84	1. `WorkspaceDashboardComponent` reads `DashboardLayoutService.state()`.
85	2. Enabled widgets are filtered and rendered in layout order.
86	3. `DashboardWidgetHostComponent` maps `widget.type` to a concrete widget
87	   component.
88	4. Widgets receive the normalized config, including size and optional scope.
89	5. Data comes from `DashboardDataService` and existing provider/state services.
90	6. Widget actions deep-link back into workspace/provider routes.
91	
92	Dashboard detail handoff contract:
93	
94	1. Live items continue to activate their existing playback/provider route flows.
95	2. Xtream and Stalker movies/series from `global-favorites` or
96	   `recently-watched` should route into `/workspace/global-favorites` or
97	   `/workspace/global-recent` with collection detail pre-opened from navigation
98	   state.
99	3. Those collection detail opens must not switch the active playlist in the
100	   header playlist switcher.
101	4. Those collection detail opens must not show the workspace category sidebar.
102	5. The detail close/back action should return to the dashboard-origin view
103	   rather than reopening provider/category navigation.
104	
105	## Customize Mode
106	
107	Customize mode is part of the current product, not future work.
108	
109	Supported actions:
110	
111	1. Toggle widget visibility.
112	2. Drag-and-drop reorder for visible widgets.
113	3. Change widget size within the fixed preset list.
114	4. Configure provider scope for scoped widgets.
115	5. Configure playlist scope for scoped widgets.
116	6. Reset the layout to defaults.
117	
118	Scope-aware widgets currently rely on a provider/playlist filter model rather
119	than per-widget custom query systems.
120	
121	## UX Rules
122	
123	1. Widgets should represent user tasks, not provider internals.
124	2. Each widget must own its loading, empty, and error states.
125	3. Dashboard failures must stay isolated to the widget that failed.
126	4. Widget navigation should resolve directly into the relevant content context.
127	5. Dashboard favorites/recent movie/series activations should preserve the
128	   current playlist context and use the collection-owned detail host instead of
129	   forcing provider/category side-navigation.
130	6. New widgets should fit the existing constrained layout model unless the
131	   dashboard architecture is explicitly being expanded.
132	
133	## Adding Or Changing Widgets
134	
135	Current workflow:
136	
137	1. Add or update the widget type in `dashboard-widget.model.ts`.
138	2. Implement the widget UI under `libs/workspace/dashboard/ui/src/lib/widgets/`.
139	3. Register the widget in `dashboard-widget-host.component.ts`.
140	4. Add default state and migration-safe behavior in
141	   `dashboard-layout.service.ts`.
142	5. Extend `dashboard-data.service.ts` or reuse an existing feature service.
143	6. Ensure the widget has explicit empty/error/loading states and valid
144	   workspace deep links.
145	
146	## Deferred Work
147	
148	These items are intentionally not part of the current contract:
149	
150	1. Freeform drag/resize grid with collision management.
151	2. External data widgets such as RSS, sports, or news adapters.

# Workspace Dashboard

This document records the current dashboard implementation inside the workspace
shell.

Related:

- [Workspace Shell](./workspace-shell.md)

## Summary

- The dashboard is the default `/workspace` landing page.
- It is a **rail-based** content surface (Netflix / Apple TV pattern), not a
  customizable widget grid.
- Layout is static and curated — there is no edit mode, drag-drop, size
  stepper, show/hide toggle, or persisted layout. Rails auto-hide when empty.
- First-run users see the shared welcome empty-state with a single primary
  CTA to add their first playlist.

Core implementation:

1. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/rails/workspace-dashboard-rails.component.ts`
   — the page-level facade.
2. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/rails/dashboard-rail.component.ts`
   — the reusable horizontal rail.
3. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-data.service.ts`
   — data aggregation (recent items, favorites, playlist stats). Shared across
   rails.
4. `libs/playlist/shared/ui/src/lib/recent-playlists/empty-state/empty-state.component.ts`
   — reused welcome state with the primary "Add your first playlist" CTA.

## Page Structure

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  Hero — Continue Watching (most recent item)                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Recently Watched · See all →                                       │
│  [poster][poster][poster][poster] →→                                │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Global Favorites · See all →                                       │
│  [poster][poster][poster] →→                                        │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│  Recent Sources · See all →                                         │
│  [tile][tile][tile][tile] →→                                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

Render rules:

1. `hasPlaylists() === false` → render `<app-empty-state type="welcome">`
   full-bleed. All rails and the hero are skipped.
2. `hero()` = `globalRecentItems()[0]`. If present, render the hero panel.
3. Each rail is emitted via `@if (cards.length > 0)`. Empty rails are hidden
   — there is no "empty widget" placeholder.

## Rail Contract

`DashboardRailComponent` is purely presentational:

1. Inputs: `label`, `items: DashboardRailCard[]`, optional `seeAllLink`,
   optional `aspectRatio` (default `'2 / 3'`).
2. Behavior: horizontal flex track with `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`.
3. Chevron buttons fade in on hover (desktop only via `@media (hover: none)`).
4. Cards are keyboard-focusable router links; `scroll-snap-align: start`
   means arrow-key nav lands on card boundaries.
5. Image handling: `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`, fallback icon tile
   when `imageUrl` is missing or `error` fires.

## Data Flow

1. `WorkspaceDashboardRailsComponent` injects `DashboardDataService` (kept
   unchanged from the previous dashboard).
2. It derives four signals via `computed()`:
    1. `hero` — first item of `globalRecentItems()`.
    2. `recentlyWatchedCards` — maps `globalRecentItems()` to rail cards.
    3. `favoriteCards` — maps `globalFavoriteItems()` to rail cards.
    4. `sourceCards` — maps `recentPlaylists()` to rail cards.
3. No `Layout` state, no localStorage keys, no migrations.
4. Navigation state + deep-link targets come from the existing
   `getRecentItemLink()` / `getGlobalFavoriteLink()` / `getPlaylistLink()`
   helpers on `DashboardDataService` and reuse the workspace navigation
   helpers in `@iptvnator/portal/shared/util`.

## Empty State

The welcome state is rendered via the existing
`EmptyStateComponent` (`type="welcome"`) from
`libs/playlist/shared/ui`:

1. Illustration + headline + description from the existing M3U welcome
   strings (`HOME.PLAYLISTS.WELCOME_*`).
2. Primary button emits `addPlaylistClicked`. The dashboard page wires this
   to `WORKSPACE_SHELL_ACTIONS.openAddPlaylistDialog()`.
3. Feature chips (M3U / Xtream / Stalker) are provided by the component.

## UX Rules

1. Rails represent content the user is likely to resume, not provider
   internals. Never surface raw API objects.
2. Each rail must auto-hide when its data source is empty.
3. Image assets must degrade to a typed icon fallback — never show broken
   images or empty tiles.
4. The page must never show "No widgets" style text. If there is no content
   and no playlists, render the welcome state; otherwise render whatever
   rails have data.
5. Navigation from a rail card must deep-link into the appropriate workspace
   route without switching the active playlist in the header switcher.

## Adding Or Changing Rails

Current workflow:

1. Add a new `computed()` signal for the card list in
   `WorkspaceDashboardRailsComponent`, mapping your source data to
   `DashboardRailCard`.
2. Drop a `<lib-dashboard-rail>` in the template, gated by
   `@if (cards.length > 0)`.
3. If the data source is new, extend `DashboardDataService` rather than
   reaching into DB services directly from the component.
4. Provide a `seeAllLink` only if there is a dedicated "manage all" route
   for that content type.

## Deferred Work

Intentionally out of scope:

1. Customizable layout (drag/drop, resize, show/hide toggles, layout
   persistence). Removed in favor of a curated, opinionated order.
2. Freeform widget grid with collision management.
3. External data rails such as RSS, sports, or news adapters.
4. Per-user A/B variants of rail ordering.

# Workspace Dashboard

This document records the current dashboard implementation inside the workspace
shell. It replaces the earlier dashboard plan document.

Related:

- [Workspace Shell](./workspace-shell.md)

## Summary

- The dashboard is the default `/workspace` landing page.
- It is a widget-based surface with persisted layout and widget settings.
- The current implementation favors a constrained, stable layout over a full
  freeform grid system.

Core implementation:

1. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/workspace-dashboard.component.ts`
2. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/workspace-dashboard.component.html`
3. `libs/workspace/dashboard/ui/src/lib/dashboard-widget-host.component.ts`
4. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-widget.model.ts`
5. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-layout.service.ts`
6. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-data.service.ts`

## Current Widget Set

Registered widget types:

1. `source-stats`
2. `continue-watching`
3. `recently-watched`
4. `global-favorites`

Default layout:

1. `continue-watching`
    1. Enabled by default
    2. Size `full`
2. `recently-watched`
    1. Enabled by default
    2. Size `two-thirds`
    3. Scope-aware
3. `global-favorites`
    1. Enabled by default
    2. Size `one-third`
    3. Scope-aware
4. `source-stats`
    1. Present in the registry
    2. Disabled by default
    3. Size `one-third`

The old refactor summary mentioned `Recent Sources`, but that widget is not in
the current registry and should not be documented as shipped behavior.

## Layout And Persistence Contract

The dashboard persists a versioned layout object in local storage.

Current storage details:

1. Storage key: `workspace-dashboard-layout-v3`
2. Schema version: `12`
3. Size presets:
    1. `one-third`
    2. `half`
    3. `two-thirds`
    4. `full`
4. Scope settings:
    1. `providers: Array<'m3u' | 'xtream' | 'stalker'>`
    2. `playlistIds: string[]`

Normalization rules in `DashboardLayoutService`:

1. Stored widgets are merged against `DEFAULT_DASHBOARD_WIDGETS`.
2. Missing widgets are restored from defaults.
3. Removed or invalid settings fall back to normalized defaults.
4. Titles and descriptions come from the current code-defined defaults, not
   stale stored values.
5. Widget order is reindexed after normalization.

## Rendering Flow

1. `WorkspaceDashboardComponent` reads `DashboardLayoutService.state()`.
2. Enabled widgets are filtered and rendered in layout order.
3. `DashboardWidgetHostComponent` maps `widget.type` to a concrete widget
   component.
4. Widgets receive the normalized config, including size and optional scope.
5. Data comes from `DashboardDataService` and existing provider/state services.
6. Widget actions deep-link back into workspace/provider routes.

Dashboard detail handoff contract:

1. Live items continue to activate their existing playback/provider route flows.
2. Xtream and Stalker movies/series from `global-favorites` or
   `recently-watched` should route into `/workspace/global-favorites` or
   `/workspace/global-recent` with collection detail pre-opened from navigation
   state.
3. Those collection detail opens must not switch the active playlist in the
   header playlist switcher.
4. Those collection detail opens must not show the workspace category sidebar.
5. The detail close/back action should return to the dashboard-origin view
   rather than reopening provider/category navigation.

## Customize Mode

Customize mode is part of the current product, not future work.

Supported actions:

1. Toggle widget visibility.
2. Drag-and-drop reorder for visible widgets.
3. Change widget size within the fixed preset list.
4. Configure provider scope for scoped widgets.
5. Configure playlist scope for scoped widgets.
6. Reset the layout to defaults.

Scope-aware widgets currently rely on a provider/playlist filter model rather
than per-widget custom query systems.

## UX Rules

1. Widgets should represent user tasks, not provider internals.
2. Each widget must own its loading, empty, and error states.
3. Dashboard failures must stay isolated to the widget that failed.
4. Widget navigation should resolve directly into the relevant content context.
5. Dashboard favorites/recent movie/series activations should preserve the
   current playlist context and use the collection-owned detail host instead of
   forcing provider/category side-navigation.
6. New widgets should fit the existing constrained layout model unless the
   dashboard architecture is explicitly being expanded.

## Adding Or Changing Widgets

Current workflow:

1. Add or update the widget type in `dashboard-widget.model.ts`.
2. Implement the widget UI under `libs/workspace/dashboard/ui/src/lib/widgets/`.
3. Register the widget in `dashboard-widget-host.component.ts`.
4. Add default state and migration-safe behavior in
   `dashboard-layout.service.ts`.
5. Extend `dashboard-data.service.ts` or reuse an existing feature service.
6. Ensure the widget has explicit empty/error/loading states and valid
   workspace deep links.

## Deferred Work

These items are intentionally not part of the current contract:

1. Freeform drag/resize grid with collision management.
2. External data widgets such as RSS, sports, or news adapters.
3. A widget marketplace or plugin system.

content.text:
Both issues fixed.

**1. Card width variance** — Real CSS bug. Flex items default to `min-width: auto` (intrinsic content size), which overrode my `flex-basis: 172px` whenever a title was longer than the card. Added `min-width: 0; width: var(--rail-card-width); max-width: var(--rail-card-width);` to `.rail__card`. All 110 cards now render at exactly 172px; long titles like "Brazzers TV Europe Россия" truncate with ellipsis as designed. Change in [dashboard-rail.component.scss](libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/rails/dashboard-rail.component.scss).

**2. Resize regression** — Not a code regression. My earlier `agent-browser set viewport …` commands during testing sent `Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride` to the Electron target, which *pins* the viewport until explicitly cleared — your window drag was being overridden by the CDP emulation. Cleared it via a direct `Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride` CDP call; native window resize now takes effect. (Going forward I'll avoid `set viewport` and stick to manipulating `Browser.setWindowBounds` or just taking screenshots at whatever size you've set.)

Window currently at 1280×820, hero 300px+796px grid, cards uniformly 172px. Try dragging the window — it should now reflow as expected.

content.text:
Here's the plan — grounded in what I found in the code.

## What's actually happening

The duplication is real and structural. Today the rail has two Favorites entries that route to **the same underlying component** but with different inputs:

| Rail entry | Route | `playlistId` passed? | Scope toggle visible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Top ❤️ "Global favorites" (my addition) | `/workspace/global-favorites` | ❌ | ❌ forced to "all" |
| Bottom ❤️ "Favorites (this playlist)" | `/workspace/[provider]/[id]/favorites` | ✅ | ✅ "This playlist / All playlists" |

Relevant code: [`showScopeToggle = computed(() => Boolean(this.playlistId()))`](libs/portal/shared/ui/src/lib/components/unified-collection/unified-collection-page.component.ts:182). Same story for Recent (🕓).

## What users actually want (brainstorm lens)

Three tasks, one concept: "show me my favorites, scoped however makes sense right now."

1. *No playlist active* → "all playlists" view
2. *Playlist active* → "this playlist" view, with option to widen
3. *Power user* → flip between scopes mid-session

Today we answer #1 and #2 with separate rail entries, and #3 with the inline toggle. The rail duplication is paying twice for something the inline toggle already solves.

## Design principles at stake (design lens)

- **Rail icons should be stable across navigation.** Icons appearing/disappearing when you click into a playlist breaks the spatial map.
- **Identical icons twice (two ❤️, two 🕓) is the worst outcome** — users can't distinguish without hovering. This is a textbook duplication smell.
- **Global concepts live at the top of the rail, per-context at the bottom.** The project already uses this pattern — the fix is to honor it, not fight it.
- **One entry point + context-aware default scope** is the Apple TV / Spotify / Netflix pattern. Proven, learnable, not novel.

## Recommendation: unify to one entry each, context-aware default

**Change 1 — Remove duplicates from the per-playlist rail.** Strip `favorites` and `recent` from `buildPortalRailLinks()` in [portal-rail-links.ts](libs/portal/shared/util/src/lib/navigation/portal-rail-links.ts) (all three providers: xtreams, stalker, playlists). The bottom rail keeps what is *only* meaningful in playlist context: All / Groups / VOD / Live / Series / Search / Downloads / Recently-added.

**Change 2 — Context-aware default scope on the global routes.** Teach [`GlobalCollectionRouteComponent`](apps/web/src/app/global-collection-route.component.ts) to read the active playlist from the workspace facade. When a playlist is active, pass its `playlistId` down to `<app-unified-collection-page>` — this flips `showScopeToggle` to true and defaults the scope to "This playlist." When no playlist is active, no toggle, "all playlists" as today.

**Result**:
- Four stable top-rail icons at all times (Dashboard, Sources, Favorites, Recent) — no state-based visibility.
- Click ❤️ with no playlist active → "All playlists" favorites, no toggle.
- Click ❤️ with a playlist active → "This playlist" favorites by default, toggle visible, one click widens to All.
- Zero icon duplication, zero functional regression for the "this playlist's favorites" case.

## Tradeoffs I considered and rejected

- **Hide top globals when playlist is selected** — breaks rail stability, worst of both worlds.
- **Visual differentiation (outlined vs filled icons)** — papers over duplication, doesn't solve the mental-model problem.
- **Retire the per-playlist `/playlists/:id/favorites` and `/[provider]/:id/favorites` routes entirely** — cleaner but much bigger, touches deep-links and existing navigation helpers. I'd do it as a separate follow-up.

## Scope estimate

About 15–25 lines of real change across 2 files:
- `portal-rail-links.ts`: remove 6 entries (favorites + recent across xtreams / stalker / playlists)
- `global-collection-route.component.ts`: inject the workspace facade, compute `playlistId` from `activePlaylist()`, pass it through

Plus i18n is untouched, routing is untouched. Lint and the existing scope-toggle tests should still pass.

Want me to go? Or do you want me to preserve the per-playlist routes (and just remove the rail entries that point to them) in case anything deep-links to them externally?

Done. Both issues addressed using the pattern from [content-hero.component](libs/ui/components/src/lib/content-hero/content-hero.component.scss:92) that's already proven in the VOD/series detail view.

## What changed

**Issue 1 — poster cropping**: The hero no longer stretches the portrait poster into a 16:9 frame. The poster renders in its native **2:3 aspect** in a sharp 160×240 card (120px on mobile), matching exactly how the same asset looks in the Recently Watched rail — no more cut-off faces.

**Issue 2 — boring flat background**: Mirrored the content-hero's 3-layer composition:

- **Layer 0 — backdrop**: the poster image itself, reused as a blurred backdrop (`filter: blur(36px) saturate(1.25); transform: scale(1.35); opacity: 0.55`). Scale 1.35 keeps the blurred edges off-screen. Same technique as `.hero__backdrop--blurred` in content-hero.
- **Layer 1 — vignette**: horizontal `color-mix` gradient in the app's surface color — darker on the far left (where the poster sits) and far right (behind the CTA) for contrast, lighter in the middle. Plus a soft top-to-bottom fade.
- **Layer 2 — content**: the sharp 2:3 poster card + text block. Title and eyebrow get stronger contrast (`text-shadow` + white title) only when a backdrop image is present — the fallback no-image state keeps the current accent-gradient look.

**Fallback**: if `poster_url` is absent, the `.hero--with-image` class is not applied — `.hero:not(.hero--with-image)` falls back to the accent gradient, no empty backdrop layer, and the poster card shows the icon fallback (same as before).

**Accessibility**: backdrop + vignette have `aria-hidden="true"` and `pointer-events: none`, so the entire hero remains a single clickable anchor + screen readers get only the meaningful title/eyebrow/subtitle.

**Responsive**: `--hero-poster-width` drops from 160 → 120px under 720px width; grid stays 2-column (poster + body) so the layout doesn't collapse awkwardly.

Lint passes. CDP is still down so I couldn't screenshot live — please restart Electron to see it. The Krypton cover should now render as a sharp upright poster on the left with a blurred Krypton-red wash filling the whole hero panel behind it, instead of the current cropped 16:9 tile on the flat purple background.

content.text:
Screenshot verification — the tuned backdrop now reads cinematically:

![tuned hero](file:///tmp/iptv-hero-tuned.png)

The Krypton poster's red-to-pink palette bleeds across the whole hero panel as a soft wash. Title + "Continue Watching" CTA stay legible because the vignette keeps a subtle scrim behind the text (right-edge ~65% surface) while the middle sits at only ~10% — letting the image breathe.

## What changed (visual only, no data-layer changes)
- `opacity: 0.55 → 0.9` on the backdrop — poster's colour actually shows now.
- `blur: 36px → 40px`, `saturate: 1.25 → 1.5`, `scale: 1.35 → 1.5` — matches content-hero's fallback intensity.
- Vignette re-balanced: **55%** surface behind the poster card (preserves card contrast), **10%** across the middle, **65%** behind the CTA (preserves text legibility). Middle no longer dominates.
- Added a soft bottom fade (55% transparent → 35% surface) so the hero melds into the rails below.

## What I did NOT do (needs your call)

**Real backdrop URLs from the Xtream API are not available in this data path.** I traced it:
- The `content` DB table has only `poster_url`, no `backdrop_url` column — [libs/shared/database/src/lib/schema.ts:89](libs/shared/database/src/lib/schema.ts:89).
- `backdrop_path` is fetched ad-hoc by [vod-details-adapters.ts:22](libs/shared/interfaces/src/lib/vod-details-adapters.ts:22) when the user opens the detail view. It's never persisted.
- The recent/favorites queries ([favorites.operations.ts:121](apps/electron-backend/src/app/database/operations/favorites.operations.ts:121), [recently-viewed.operations.ts](apps/electron-backend/src/app/database/operations/recently-viewed.operations.ts)) select `content.posterUrl` only.

To surface the real backdrop like vod-details does, we'd need one of:

**A — Persist it**: add `backdropUrl` column to `content`, populate when detail view fetches info (or during xtream sync), migrate existing DBs via `ALTER TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` in `connection.ts`. ~6 files. Existing DBs populate progressively as users view details.

**B — Lazy-fetch on dashboard load**: inject `XtreamApiService` into `DashboardDataService`, cache `getVodInfo`/`getSeriesInfo` for the hero item, pipe `backdrop_path[0]` into the hero. ~3 files. One network call per dashboard open; graceful fallback to blurred poster if offline.

**C — Do nothing more**: the tuned blurred-poster backdrop is good enough for a dashboard hero. The real backdrop is a "nice-to-have" only visible when clicking into the detail view.

My recommendation: **C for now**, because the tuned blurred version already delivers the cinematic vibe. If you want to be thorough later, **A** is the durable answer (works offline, no repeat API calls). Want me to proceed with A, or leave it here?

5	export async function getRecentlyViewed(db: AppDatabase) {
6	    return db
7	        .select({
8	            id: schema.content.id,
9	            category_id: schema.content.categoryId,
10	            title: schema.content.title,
11	            rating: schema.content.rating,
12	            added: schema.content.added,
13	            poster_url: schema.content.posterUrl,
14	            xtream_id: schema.content.xtreamId,
15	            type: schema.content.type,
16	            playlist_id: schema.categories.playlistId,
17	            playlist_name: schema.playlists.name,
18	            viewed_at: schema.recentlyViewed.viewedAt,
19	        })
20	        .from(schema.recentlyViewed)
21	        .innerJoin(
22	            schema.content,
23	            eq(schema.recentlyViewed.contentId, schema.content.id)
24	        )
25	        .innerJoin(
26	            schema.categories,
27	            eq(schema.content.categoryId, schema.categories.id)
28	        )
29	        .innerJoin(

31	            eq(schema.categories.playlistId, schema.playlists.id)

35	}

70	export async function addRecentItem(
71	    db: AppDatabase,
72	    contentId: number,
73	    playlistId: string
74	): Promise<{ success: boolean }> {
75	    const existing = await db
76	        .select()
77	        .from(schema.recentlyViewed)
78	        .where(
79	            and(
80	                eq(schema.recentlyViewed.contentId, contentId),
81	                eq(schema.recentlyViewed.playlistId, playlistId)
82	            )
83	        )
84	        .limit(1);
85	
86	    if (existing.length > 0) {
87	        await db
88	            .update(schema.recentlyViewed)
89	            .set({ viewedAt: sql`CURRENT_TIMESTAMP` })
90	            .where(
91	                and(
92	                    eq(schema.recentlyViewed.contentId, contentId),
93	                    eq(schema.recentlyViewed.playlistId, playlistId)
94	                )
95	            );
96	    } else {
97	        await db.insert(schema.recentlyViewed).values({
98	            contentId,
99	            playlistId,
100	        });
101	    }
102	
103	    return { success: true };
104	}

Done. Lazy-persist pipeline is live end-to-end.

## What's wired

**Schema** ([schema.ts:90](libs/shared/database/src/lib/schema.ts:90) / [connection.ts:115,271](libs/shared/database/src/lib/connection.ts:271)): new `backdrop_url TEXT` column on `content`, plus an idempotent `ALTER TABLE content ADD COLUMN backdrop_url TEXT` migration that ran on your last Electron restart.

**Write paths** ([favorites.operations.ts](apps/electron-backend/src/app/database/operations/favorites.operations.ts), [recently-viewed.operations.ts](apps/electron-backend/src/app/database/operations/recently-viewed.operations.ts)): `addFavorite` + `addRecentItem` now accept an optional `backdropUrl` and only UPDATE `content.backdrop_url` when the existing value is NULL/empty — never overwrites. This is a "lazy, non-destructive" persist.

**IPC chain**: preload → events dispatcher → worker → operation, all threaded with the optional `backdropUrl`. `DatabaseService` + `XtreamDataSource` interface + both Electron/PWA implementations updated (PWA ignores the param — localStorage has no content table).

**Detail views** ([vod-details-route.component.ts:395,493](libs/portal/xtream/feature/src/lib/vod-details/vod-details-route.component.ts:493), [serial-details.component.ts:240,293](libs/portal/xtream/feature/src/lib/serial-details/serial-details.component.ts:293)): both pass `selectedVodInfo()?.backdrop_path?.[0]` / `selectedItem()?.info?.backdrop_path?.[0]` to `toggleFavorite` and `addRecentItem`. So **opening a VOD or series detail page will now save the backdrop** the first time you view it.

**Read path**: `getAllGlobalFavorites` + `getRecentlyViewed` SELECT `backdrop_url`. `mapDbRecentToItem` / `mapDbFavoriteToItem` forward it to `PortalActivityItem.backdrop_url`.

**Hero rendering** ([workspace-dashboard-rails.component.html](libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/rails/workspace-dashboard-rails.component.html), .scss): two modes —
- `.hero--has-backdrop` (real backdrop present): sharp image, `blur(2px) saturate(1.1)`, `scale(1.05)`, opacity 1, stronger pure-black vignette for text legibility.
- Fallback (only poster): `blur(40px) saturate(1.5)`, `scale(1.5)`, opacity 0.9, surface-tinted vignette — the cinematic colour wash you saw in the last screenshot.

**Stalker**: skipped. `vod-details-adapters.ts:47` comments "Stalker doesn't provide backdrop" and stalker favorites/recent use the playlist-meta array path, not the `content` table. Blurred-poster fallback applies.

## How to verify

Current dashboard shows Shark Tank in fallback mode (wash of yellow/orange poster colours). To see a real backdrop:

1. Open any xtream VOD or series detail page (e.g. click Krypton or any poster card).
2. The `addRecentItem` call from `ngOnInit` (or `toggleFavorite` if you hit the heart) now writes `backdrop_url` into `content` for that row.
3. Navigate back to `/workspace/dashboard`.
4. That item's hero now renders with sharp wide backdrop, strong vignette, `hero--has-backdrop` class applied.

Backfill happens organically as you browse — no one-time migration needed.

**Tests**: `portal-xtream-data-access` 61/61 green, `workspace-dashboard-feature` lint clean. Updated one spec assertion to account for the new `undefined` backdrop arg.

content.text:
Before coding, design take — since auto-rotation is one of the most-studied and most-regretted UX patterns.

## Industry reality check

**No major streaming app auto-rotates their hero.** Netflix, Apple TV+, Disney+, HBO, Prime — all use a static "billboard" (one item, often with a muted auto-play preview). The auto-rotating hero is a pattern from mid-2010s marketing sites (Bootstrap carousel era) and travel booking. Nielsen Norman Group has repeatedly measured that **engagement on slides 2–5 drops to single digits** and that rotating content actively hurts comprehension.

Why streaming apps don't do it:
- Rotation interrupts reading just as the user processes the title
- Cursor precision — user reaches to click → hero changes under them
- WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause/Stop/Hide) requires pause controls for any auto-animation — easy to get wrong
- You already have a "Recently Watched" rail directly below showing the same items

## When it does work

TV/10-foot UIs (Apple TV main menu does something close), kiosks, and **slow-enough** rotations (8s+) with pause-on-hover. The key design constraints if you go this route:

1. **≥8 seconds per slide** — below that, users feel rushed
2. **Pause on hover AND keyboard focus** — non-negotiable
3. **`prefers-reduced-motion` → disable entirely**
4. **Cross-fade, not slide** — less jarring
5. **Dots below CTA, clickable + keyboard-focusable**
6. **5 items max** (you had this right)
7. **First slide = last watched** — anchor, not random

## What I'd actually recommend

**Manual carousel, no auto-rotate.** Dots + arrow keys + swipe, user-driven. Keeps the hero feeling alive (5 variations of the big backdrop, one click away), removes every auto-rotation tax, matches the Netflix/Apple TV mental model.

If that feels too static, a middle path: **rotate only while the dashboard tab is idle** — pause the timer whenever the user moves the mouse inside the hero, clicks a dot, or focuses anywhere on the page. Restart after 15s of inactivity. This is how some TV dashboards behave and sidesteps the "rotated while I was reading" problem.

## My vote

Ship the **manual carousel** now (≈30 min of work), gate auto-rotate behind a setting (`Settings → Dashboard → Auto-rotate hero`, default off) if you want it later. That way power users can opt in, but the default matches streaming-app conventions and is accessible out of the box.

Which direction do you want?
1. Manual carousel only (arrows + dots + swipe + keyboard), no auto
2. Manual carousel + optional auto-rotate (pause on hover + prefers-reduced-motion + settings toggle)
3. Full auto-rotate as you described (I'll implement with all the accessibility guards)

content.text:
Current numbers:

| Source | Limit | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| DB query (xtream recent) | 100 | `getRecentlyViewed` |
| DB query (xtream favorites) | 500 | `getAllGlobalFavorites` |
| `globalRecentItems` (combined) | 200 | Dashboard rails + hero |
| `globalFavoriteItems` (combined) | 200 | Dashboard rails |
| Rail renders | **All 200** | `recentlyWatchedCards`/`favoriteCards` map the whole set |

So the Recently Watched rail currently dumps up to **200 card components into the DOM**, even though only ~7 are visible at any time and "Manage all" is right there for the full list.

Real cost: DOM nodes + layout work. Image fetches are lazy (`loading="lazy"`), so off-screen images don't download. But with 200 cards, Angular still creates 200 signal evaluations, 200 `@for` iterations, 200 anchor+img trees.

## Recommendation

Cap the **rail** (not the underlying data service) at 20 items. Keep the service at 200 so the hero's "most recent" selection is still correct and so "Manage all" page (if it reads the same computed) gets the full set. Sources rail is already fine — `recentPlaylists()` caps at 12.

20 cards = roughly 3× visible (user sees ~7), enough for a natural "scroll past my recent stuff" feel without dumping everything. Matches what Netflix/Apple TV put in a single rail before the "See more" link.

Let me implement.

content.text:
I've got the data. Running the audit through the `/frontend-design` + UI-wiki typography lens:

**What's solid**
- Font stack: DM Sans primary, Roboto fallback — correct for UI
- Weight hierarchy: 700 (eyebrow) → 600 (titles/CTA) → 500 (body) — clean
- Color tokens from `--app-*` — consistent with the rest of the app
- Card 1-line ellipsis — matches Netflix rhythm

**What's off**
1. **`line-height: normal` on 6 of 8 text elements** — renderer-dependent, usually 1.2-1.4. Professional UIs pin explicit values for vertical consistency across macOS/Windows/Linux font renderers.
2. **Rail title 16.8px feels small** next to the 27.2px hero title — chapter markers should be more assertive. Netflix is 18px, Apple TV+ 22px.
3. **Hero title letter-spacing -0.02em is over-tightened** for 27px — that ratio is appropriate above ~48px (display type). Current rendering looks crammed.
4. **No item counts anywhere** — user asked about count badges specifically, and they're a streaming-app staple ("Recently Watched · 12", HBO Max style).
5. **"Manage all" is a bare text link** — no hover background, no clear affordance beyond colour change.
6. **CTA icon/text baseline misalignment risk** without explicit `line-height` on the pill.

Implementing the fixes now.

content.text:
Great observation. Let me audit the current state and think through it via `/frontend-design` + `/userinterface-wiki` patterns.

## What's wrong with the current chevrons

Current spec:
- 36×48 pill shape
- Background: `var(--app-widget-bg)` = `#1e2330` — **identical color to the card fallback tiles**, so they camouflage
- Only visible on viewport hover (opacity 0 at rest)
- Icon 22px
- Positioned inside the viewport (left: -4px)

Failures:
1. **Hit target**: 36×48 is below the 44×44 desktop convention and awkward for fine cursors
2. **Background contrast**: same hex as `.rail__art` fallback → fully blends when the scroll position reveals a fallback tile behind the chevron
3. **Discoverability**: fully invisible until you hover the viewport — users have to guess the scroll affordance exists
4. **Shape**: rectangle with 10px radius reads as "card-adjacent UI," not navigation. Streaming apps use circles (Netflix, Apple TV+, Spotify) precisely because they pop against any rectangular content

## Streaming-app reference patterns

- **Netflix**: 48px circle, `rgba(0,0,0,0.75)` bg, white chevron, visible-on-hover, **edge gradient fade** on the rail so the row looks like it "flows offscreen"
- **Apple TV+**: 44px circle, dark glass with heavy backdrop-blur, white icon, fades in on hover
- **Disney+**: larger 56px circle, ring of white border, more pronounced
- **YouTube**: 40px circle, semi-transparent black, always-on when scrollable

The common thread: **circle + high-contrast dark glass + white icon + show some state of themselves when scroll is possible**.

## Plan

1. **Circle shape** (44×44) — matches streaming convention, always contrasts with rectangular content
2. **`rgba(0,0,0,0.72)` background** + `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)` — works against dark posters, fallback tiles, AND bright posters (like Krypton red)
3. **1px `rgba(255,255,255,0.14)` border** — subtle edge definition
4. **White icon at 24px + soft text-shadow** — stays readable over anything
5. **Peek at rest when scrollable** (opacity 0.5), full opacity on hover — discoverability without clutter
6. **Edge gradient on the track** (20px fade from page bg on the leading/trailing edge) — cues scroll-ability even when cursor is elsewhere
7. **Hover: scale(1.08) + deeper shadow** — tactile feedback

Implementing now.

content.text:
The chevron is now clearly readable against both dark fallback tiles (Setanta/ADULTXXX6) and bright posters (NRJ red, pH orange, Krypton). Final verified spec:

| Attribute | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Shape | 36×48 pill (10px radius) | **44×44 circle** |
| Background | `#1e2330` (matches card fallback) | **`rgba(0,0,0,0.72)`** with `backdrop-filter: blur(12px)` |
| Border | outline-variant (barely visible) | **`rgba(255,255,255,0.14)`** — subtle edge definition |
| Icon | 22px, inherits body color | **24px white + drop-shadow** — stays crisp over bright content |
| At-rest when scrollable | `opacity: 0` (invisible) | **`opacity: 0.5`** — peek hint |
| On hover | `scale(1.05)` + `--app-card-hover-bg` | **`scale(1.08)` + `rgba(0,0,0,0.88)` + 4px white ring glow** |
| Active | — | `scale(0.96)` tactile feedback |
| Focus | none | **2px accent-blue ring, 3px offset** |
| Edge fade | — | **32px gradient on the rail edge** when scroll is possible in that direction, using `:has()` to pair with chevron visibility |

**What this fixes**:
- **Hit target**: 44×44 is the WCAG-recommended touch size and the standard Netflix/Apple TV+ circle dimension. Easy to hit on desktop with any input device.
- **Contrast problem**: Near-black glass with heavy blur works against any underlying color — no more camouflaging with fallback tiles.
- **Discoverability**: Peek at 50% opacity when scroll is possible plus the soft edge gradient cues "there's more to the side" before the user even hovers. Previously you had to blindly hover the viewport to discover the controls.
- **Streaming conventions**: Circle shape, dark glass, white icon, edge gradient — these are the four design primitives that make Netflix/Apple TV+ rails feel like rails.
- **Keyboard accessibility**: Proper `:focus-visible` ring (was absent before); tabbing through now highlights each chevron clearly.

The edge gradient uses CSS `:has(.rail__chev--visible)` so it only appears on the side where scrolling is actually possible — when you're at the start of a rail, only the right gradient shows; at the end, only the left. No decoration when the rail is short enough to fit everything.

Lint passes. Computed styles confirmed (44×44, `border-radius: 50%`, `rgba(0,0,0,0.88)` on hover). Try hovering the rails — the chevron should feel clearly grabbable now.

Lost ~70 lines of SCSS (the old `.section`, `.carousel`, `h3` rules); gained uniform typography, count badges, chevron navigation, edge fades, and focus-visible rings. ## What matches the dashboard now - **Header scale**: 18px/600 label + muted pill count badge (true total, not capped) - **"Manage all" placement pattern**: right-aligned see-all link with pill hover (none wired on recently-added yet — it has no dedicated "all items" route, but the prop is there for when one exists) - **Chevrons**: 44×44 dark-glass circles, peek at 0.5 opacity when scroll is possible, scale 1.08 on hover, `:focus-visible` accent ring - **Edge gradients**: 32px fade from page bg on the side(s) where scroll is possible, toggled via `:has()` - **Active section accent**: kept the old selection-color halo pattern (used when the currently-viewed content type matches), applied via `.rail--active` on the shell ## Preserved behaviors - Active-section highlight when VOD/Series/Live matches the current `selectedContentType()` - 160px card width, 20-item cap (already in the TS sort/slice) - Date display and placeholder handling from `ContentCardComponent` ## One correctness fix worth noting Initially put `::ng-deep > *` in the shell for snap-align on projected cards. content.text:
Done. Lint passes on `portal-xtream-feature`. CDP was down so no live screenshot, but the changes are straightforward:

## Changes

**1. Border removed**
- Dropped `[active]="isSectionActive(...)"` from all three rail shells in the template
- Removed the unused `isSectionActive()` method and `selectedContentType` signal from the TS component

The `.rail--active` rule still exists on `ContentRailShellComponent` (for any future caller that wants it), but with no callers passing `[active]` on this page, recently-added now has clean rails with no selection-color halo.

**2. Skeletons added**
- New computed `isLoading()` = `(isLoadingContent || isLoadingCategories || isImporting) && no items across all three sections`. Partial-load states aren't masked — once one section resolves, real content wins over the skeletons.
- Template branches: `@if (isLoading()) { 3 skeleton rails } @else { ... }`
- Each skeleton rail matches the shell's shape: 180×22 header placeholder + 6 × 160×240 (2:3) card placeholders in a flex track
- Same shimmer animation as the dashboard (gradient sweep over `--app-widget-bg` → `--app-widget-header-bg` at 1.6s)
- Respects `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` — static gradient instead of animation
- Mobile breakpoint mirrors dashboard: card shrinks to 136px under 720px width

## Why this layout choice

Sized the skeletons to the **final content dimensions** (160×240 cards, 12px radius, 22px header) so the page doesn't reflow when real data arrives. No layout shift, which matters under slow networks where the skeleton might stay up for seconds. Six card placeholders fill a typical ~1400px viewport's horizontal row, so the overflow behavior also matches the real rail.

Not wired: a "no content at all" empty state if the user has an Xtream playlist with genuinely zero items. Right now the page would render just the title. Happy to add one — let me know.

content.text:
Done. Each recently-added rail now gets a contextual "Browse all" link routing to its type section.

## What's wired

**Shared shell** now accepts an optional `seeAllLabel` input (already-translated string). If not supplied, it falls back to the existing `WORKSPACE.DASHBOARD.MANAGE_ALL` translation — dashboard callers keep working unchanged.

**Recently-added** now passes:

| Rail | Label | Link target |
|---|---|---|
| Movies | "Browse all movies" | `/workspace/xtreams/{id}/vod` |
| Series | "Browse all series" | `/workspace/xtreams/{id}/series` |
| Live TV | "Browse all live TV" | `/workspace/xtreams/{id}/live` |

**i18n**: three new keys added to `en.json` under `PORTALS`:
- `BROWSE_ALL_MOVIES`: "Browse all movies"
- `BROWSE_ALL_SERIES`: "Browse all series"
- `BROWSE_ALL_LIVE`: "Browse all live TV"

Other locales fall back to `en` via ngx-translate default behavior.

## Implementation notes

- **Playlist id comes from `xtreamStore.currentPlaylist()?.id`**, computed reactively. If the user switches playlists, the rail links re-point without a component remount.
- **Absolute routes** used (not relative) so the links work regardless of where the router resolves from. Guards against drift if the recently-added route moves under a different parent in the future.
- **Language-aware labels**: wired a `languageTick` signal subscribed to `TranslateService.onLangChange` so the button labels re-translate when the user switches language mid-session. Matches the pattern used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `ContentCardComponent`).
- **No label duplication with rail title**: rail header says "Movies"/"Series"/"Live TV" — the button says "Browse all movies"/etc. Slight redundancy on purpose, because the button needs to stand alone if a user is hovering (the header scans as a section marker, the button as a verb-object). "Browse" was chosen over "View" / "See" / "Manage" because it implies active exploration (find something new) rather than passive consumption — matches the intent of leaving the recently-added snapshot to see the full catalog.

## What's next, if you want

- Wire similar see-all links on the Stalker portal's equivalent "New" / "Recently added" screens (if any)
- Hero-style "Continue" CTA on the top rail that uses the same pill treatment as "Browse all"

content.text:
Done. Lint passes. CDP was down so I couldn't live-screenshot, but the geometry is pixel-identical to the real dashboard shell.

## What's in the ghost now

**Hero ghost** mirrors `.hero` exactly:
- Same 18px radius, same `--app-widget-header-bg` surface + border
- Same 2-column grid: `minmax(0, 160px) minmax(0, 1fr)` with 24px gap and 20px padding
- Poster placeholder: 160×240 (2:3) with 12px radius — same as `.hero__poster`
- Body stack: 140×12 eyebrow, 60% + 35% width title bars (two lines), 45% subtitle, 160×36 pill CTA at the bottom
- Mobile (<720px) matches the real hero's 120px poster collapse

**Rail ghosts × 3** mirror `.rail`:
- 180×22 header bar (same size as the real rail title + count badge combined)
- 6 card placeholders at exactly 172×258 (matches `--rail-card-width: 172px` + 2:3 aspect on `.rail__art`)
- 14px gap, same flex layout, same overflow-hidden
- Mobile shrinks cards to 140px matching the real rail's media query

## Engineering polish

- **Shared shimmer via SCSS placeholder** (`%skeleton-shimmer`): one animation definition, one gradient, extended by 8 selectors. The compiled CSS groups them into a single rule so the browser keyframes are registered once.
- **`prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` respected**: animation disabled, static gradient stays. Matches the recently-added skeleton's accessibility behavior.
- **Zero layout shift**: card widths, aspect ratios, radii, padding, and grid template all identical to the real components. When data swaps in, elements slide in place without reflow.
- **`aria-busy="true"` + `aria-hidden="true"`** on both the hero ghost and each rail ghost so screen readers announce "busy" without reading the placeholder shapes.

## What you'll see at reload

1. Page structure appears immediately with shimmering ghost hero + 3 ghost rails
2. Data resolves → `ready()` flips true → real components fade in at the exact same dimensions
3. No jump, no flash, no "empty page" moment

Both dashboard and recently-added now share the same skeleton vocabulary (172/140/160px card widths, 2:3 aspect, 1.6s shimmer, surface/header gradient palette) so the loading experience feels like one designed system across the app.

1	# Workspace Dashboard
2	
3	This document records the current dashboard implementation inside the workspace
4	shell.
5	
6	Related:
7	
8	- [Workspace Shell](./workspace-shell.md)
9	
10	## Summary
11	
12	- The dashboard is the default `/workspace` landing page.
13	- It is a **rail-based** content surface (Netflix / Apple TV pattern), not a
14	  customizable widget grid.
15	- Layout is static and curated — there is no edit mode, drag-drop, size
16	  stepper, show/hide toggle, or persisted layout. Rails auto-hide when empty.
17	- First-run users see the shared welcome empty-state with a single primary
18	  CTA to add their first playlist.
19	
20	Core implementation:
21	
22	1. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/rails/workspace-dashboard-rails.component.ts`
23	   — the page-level facade.
24	2. `libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/rails/dashboard-rail.component.ts`
25	   — the reusable horizontal rail.
26	3. `libs/workspace/dashboard/data-access/src/lib/dashboard-data.service.ts`
27	   — data aggregation (recent items, favorites, playlist stats). Shared across
28	   rails.
29	4. `libs/playlist/shared/ui/src/lib/recent-playlists/empty-state/empty-state.component.ts`
30	   — reused welcome state with the primary "Add your first playlist" CTA.
31	
32	## Page Structure
33	
34	```
35	┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
36	│  Hero — Continue Watching (most recent item)                        │
37	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
38	│  Recently Watched · See all →                                       │
39	│  [poster][poster][poster][poster] →→                                │
40	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
41	│  Global Favorites · See all →                                       │
42	│  [poster][poster][poster] →→                                        │
43	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
44	│  Recently Used Sources · See all →                                  │
45	│  [tile][tile][tile][tile] →→                                        │
46	├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
47	│  Recently Added on Xtream (aggregated across providers)             │
48	│  [poster][poster][poster] →→                                        │
49	└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
50	```
51	
52	Render rules:
53	
54	1. `dashboardReady() === false` → render the page-level skeleton rails/hero.
55	   The first-load gate waits for playlist metadata plus the first global
56	   recent/global favorites reloads and, when Xtream playlists exist, the first
57	   Xtream recently-added reload.
58	2. `hasPlaylists() === false` → render `<app-empty-state type="welcome">`
59	   full-bleed. All rails and the hero are skipped.
60	3. `hero()` = `globalRecentItems()[0]`. If present, render the hero panel.
61	4. Each rail is emitted via `@if (cards.length > 0)`. Empty rails are hidden
62	   — there is no "empty widget" placeholder.
63	5. The continue-watching hero prefers a stored Xtream `backdrop_url`; when it
64	   is missing the UI falls back to a blurred poster treatment instead of
65	   showing a flat panel.
66	
67	## Rail Contract
68	
69	`DashboardRailComponent` is purely presentational:
70	
71	1. Inputs: `label`, `items: DashboardRailCard[]`, optional `seeAllLink`,
72	   optional `aspectRatio` (default `'2 / 3'`), optional `testId`.
73	2. Behavior: horizontal flex track with `scroll-snap-type: x mandatory`.
74	3. Chevron buttons fade in on hover (desktop only via `@media (hover: none)`).
75	4. Cards are keyboard-focusable router links; `scroll-snap-align: start`
76	   means arrow-key nav lands on card boundaries.
77	5. Image handling: `loading="lazy"`, `decoding="async"`, fallback icon tile
78	   when `imageUrl` is missing or `error` fires.
79	6. Dashboard hero, rail containers, rail cards, and "Manage all" links expose
80	   stable `data-test-id` hooks. Treat these as the supported Electron E2E
81	   selector surface; do not target internal CSS class names.
82	
83	## Data Flow
84	
85	1. `WorkspaceDashboardRailsComponent` injects `DashboardDataService`.
86	2. It derives five signals via `computed()`:
87	    1. `hero` — first item of `globalRecentItems()`.
88	    2. `recentlyWatchedCards` — maps `globalRecentItems()` to rail cards.
89	    3. `xtreamRecentlyAddedCards` — maps `xtreamRecentlyAddedItems()` to rail
90	       cards. Aggregates newly added VOD and series across *all* Xtream
91	       playlists via `DashboardDataService.reloadXtreamRecentlyAddedItems()`,
92	       which calls `getGlobalRecentlyAdded('all', limit, 'xtream')` with the
93	       DB-level `playlists.type = 'xtream'` filter. The rail is Electron-only
94	       (PWA returns `[]`) and auto-hides when empty, so users without Xtream
95	       playlists never see it. Cards carry a `playlist_name · type` subtitle
96	       so users can tell which provider each item came from. Driven by an
97	       effect that re-runs whenever the Xtream playlist count changes.
98	    4. `favoriteCards` — maps `globalFavoriteItems()` to rail cards.
99	    5. `sourceCards` — maps `recentPlaylists()` to rail cards. `recentPlaylists()`
100	       ranks M3U, Xtream, and Stalker sources by their latest recent activity
101	       from `globalRecentItems()`, then falls back to playlist
102	       `updateDate` / `importDate` for sources that have never been used.
103	3. `DashboardDataService` is passive on construction. The dashboard feature
104	   owns the initial reloads for recent items, favorites, and Xtream recently
105	   added rows on page entry.
106	4. No `Layout` state, no localStorage keys, no migrations.
107	5. Navigation state + deep-link targets come from the existing
108	   `getRecentItemLink()` / `getGlobalFavoriteLink()` / `getPlaylistLink()`
109	   helpers on `DashboardDataService` and reuse the workspace navigation
110	   helpers in `@iptvnator/portal/shared/util`.
111	6. Xtream VOD and series detail pages opportunistically backfill
112	   `content.backdrop_url` when metadata exposes a backdrop, but that write
113	   must not refresh recently viewed ordering by itself.
114	7. The dashboard feature triggers a fresh reload of DB-backed recent/favorite
115	   rows on dashboard entry so newly backfilled backdrop data is visible as soon
116	   as the user returns from a detail page.
117	
118	## Empty State

content.text:
Done. Lint green, change isolated to 22 lines of SCSS.

## Before vs After

**Before** (theme-dependent, backdrop-fragile):
- Colour: 70% accent-blue / 30% muted-grey mix → low contrast on pale backdrops
- `text-shadow: 0 1px 6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.4)` → designed for dark bg only; smudgy on light bg
- Two rules (`.hero__eyebrow` + `.hero--with-image &`) maintaining parallel paths

**After** (self-contained chip):
- `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55)` glass with `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` → readable over anything
- `border: 1px solid rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.14)` → subtle edge for definition
- `color: #fff` explicit → no inheritance surprises
- One rule, no theme variants, no backdrop variants

## Design rationale applied

- **Matches existing vocabulary**: same dark-glass + thin white border + backdrop-blur as the [`.rail__chev`](libs/workspace/dashboard/feature/src/lib/rails/dashboard-rail.component.scss) circles. The hero's label, the hero's CTA pill, and the rail chevrons now form a coherent "floating control" family.
- **Typography preserved**: 0.68rem (≈10.9px) / weight 700 / 0.14em tracking / uppercase — keeps the editorial eyebrow feel rather than looking like a status badge.
- **No layout shift**: `align-self: flex-start` inside the flex-column body keeps the chip left-aligned and its own width (no stretch), so the title below is not pushed down more than 2px extra vs. the previous text-only eyebrow.
- **`margin-bottom: 2px`**: tiny breathing room between chip and the title below, otherwise the title would start touching the chip's pill edge.

## Accessibility notes

- `color: #fff` on `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.55)` backdrop ≥ 8:1 contrast — well above WCAG AAA for small text.
- The `backdrop-filter: blur(8px)` gracefully degrades to just the dark semi-transparent background on browsers without backdrop-filter support (older Firefox without the flag) — still readable.
- No `text-shadow` needed → no rendering artefacts on any backdrop.

Restart/refresh your Electron window and you should see "CONTINUE WATCHING" as a small dark pill chip above the hero title, readable over both the colourful Russian-movie backdrop you showed and any bright/washed-out poster.
